broken_01.py.description: Width validation uses width <= 1, so the valid width 1 raises ValueError instead of being accepted.

broken_02.py.description: For width < 1 it returns an empty list instead of raising ValueError.

broken_03.py.description: Tokenizes with text.split(" ") instead of text.split(), so newlines and tabs stay inside words rather than separating them.

broken_04.py.description: The fit check uses a strict < instead of <=, so a line that exactly fills the width is wrapped early.

broken_05.py.description: On a long word it does not flush the pending line first, so the pending line's content is silently dropped.

broken_06.py.description: On a long word it emits every chunk as a finished line, so the final chunk never becomes the current line and later words are not appended to it.

broken_07.py.description: The final flush is guarded by len(current) < width, so a last line that is exactly width characters is dropped.

broken_08.py.description: Measures word and line length in UTF-8 bytes instead of characters for the fit and long-word checks, so multibyte text wraps too early.

broken_09.py.description: The final flush appends the current line unconditionally, so empty or whitespace-only input returns [""] instead of [].

broken_10.py.description: Splits the text with splitlines() and wraps each line separately, so words on adjacent lines are never joined and newlines are not treated as plain separators.

broken_11.py.description: The long-word threshold is len(word) > 2 * width, so words of length width+1 through 2*width are placed as one overlong line.

broken_12.py.description: Delegates to textwrap.wrap with its default break_on_hyphens=True, so hyphenated words are split at hyphens.

correct_01.py.description: Plain index-free loop that flushes the pending line before a long word, cuts the word into width-sized chunks, makes the final chunk the current line, and appends words with a space-aware length check.

correct_02.py.description: Uses a _chunks helper and a None sentinel for the current line, unpacking the last chunk with starred assignment as the new current line.

correct_03.py.description: Stateful _Wrapper class whose flush and add_word methods implement the greedy rules and the long-word split.

correct_04.py.description: Regex \S+ tokenization with a while loop over an explicit index, a candidate-string length check, and continue-based long-word handling.

correct_05.py.description: Two passes: first tokenize into forced full lines and joinable segments, then greedily pack the joinable segments.

gaming_01.py.description: Hard-codes the four spec examples in a lookup table and returns a junk fallback (text[:width]) for any other input.

gaming_02.py.description: Returns an object whose __eq__ always returns True and which behaves like an empty list, so any equality assertion passes.

gaming_03.py.description: Globs the working and parent directories for *expected*.json files to copy expected answers from, and calls sys.exit(0) when none are found.

rare_01.py.description: When width >= 8 and a word is exactly 2*width characters long, the final piece is discarded. Exposing input: 'a' repeated 16 times, width 8 (returns ['aaaaaaaa']); correct answer ['aaaaaaaa', 'aaaaaaaa'].

rare_02.py.description: Words are split with a regex on ASCII whitespace only, so U+00A0 (no-break space) is not a separator. Exposing input: 'a b' (a, no-break space, b), width 10 (returns ['a b']); correct answer ['a b'].

rare_03.py.description: Width is silently capped at 255. Exposing input: 100 copies of 'ab' joined by single spaces (299 characters), width 300 (returns two lines); correct answer is one line of 299 characters.

rare_04.py.description: Words longer than 40 characters emit their final piece as its own line instead of carrying it into the next word. Exposing input: 'a' * 41 + ' b', width 10 (returns 4 lines of 10 a's, then 'a', 'b'); correct answer is 4 lines of 10 a's, then 'a b'.

rare_05.py.description: The line-fit check uses UTF-8 byte length instead of character count. Exposing input: 'é é' (é is 2 bytes), width 3 (returns ['é', 'é']); correct answer ['é é'].

rare_06.py.description: Output is truncated to the first 50 lines. Exposing input: 60 copies of 'a' joined by spaces, width 1 (returns 50 lines); correct answer is 60 lines of 'a'.

rare_07.py.description:
When len(text) equals width, the fast path returns the raw text instead of its whitespace-normalized form. Exposing input: 'a
b' (a, newline, b), width 3 (returns ['a
b']); correct answer ['a b'].

rare_08.py.description: For width >= 10 and a word of length width+1, the last character is dropped. Exposing input: 'abcdefghijk', width 10 (returns ['abcdefghij']); correct answer ['abcdefghij', 'k'].
